skill.name: at-dispatch-v2
skill.description: Convert PyTorch AT_DISPATCH macros to AT_DISPATCH_V2 format in ATen C++ code. Use when porting AT_DISPATCH_ALL_TYPES_AND*, AT_DISPATCH_FLOATING_TYPES*, or other dispatch macros to the new v2 API. For ATen kernel files, CUDA kernels, and native operator implementations.
skill.summary: Convert legacy PyTorch AT_DISPATCH macros into correct AT_DISPATCH_V2 calls for ATen and CUDA kernels.
skill.author: pytorch

security_audit.summary: All 58 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around C++ identifiers and fenced examples. SKILL.md contains conversion guidance and file-editing steps, but no Ruby, shell command, external process, network request, credential handling, or prompt injection. No security remediation is required.

static_findings.snippet: This skill helps convert PyTorch's legacy AT_DISPATCH macros to the new AT_DISPATCH_V2 format, as de
- Working with files in `aten/src/ATen/native/` that use dispatch macros
1. **Reorder arguments**: `scalar_type` and `name` come first, then lambda, then types
2. **Wrap the lambda**: Use `AT_WRAP(lambda)` to handle internal commas
3. **Expand type groups**: Use `AT_EXPAND(AT_ALL_TYPES)` instead of implicit expansion
Add the v2 header near the existing `#include <ATen/Dispatch.h>`:
For combined patterns, use multiple `AT_EXPAND()` entries:
From `AT_DISPATCH_*_AND2(type1, type2, ...)` or `AT_DISPATCH_*_AND3(type1, type2, type3, ...)`, extr
2. **Composable type sets**: Mix and match type groups with `AT_EXPAND()`
- Keep `#include <ATen/Dispatch.h>` - other code may need it
- The `AT_WRAP()` is mandatory - prevents comma parsing issues in the lambda
- Type groups need `AT_EXPAND()`, individual types don't
- The v2 API is in `aten/src/ATen/Dispatch_v2.h` - refer to it for full docs

content.user_title: Convert PyTorch Dispatch Macros to V2
content.value_statement: Legacy PyTorch dispatch macros require careful argument and type-group changes. This skill converts them to AT_DISPATCH_V2 with the required include, wrappers, and explicit types.
actual_capabilities: Converts common legacy AT_DISPATCH macro families to AT_DISPATCH_V2.
Reorders scalar type, operation name, lambda, type groups, and individual types.
Wraps dispatch lambdas with AT_WRAP to preserve internal commas.
Maps legacy type families to explicit AT_EXPAND type groups.
Preserves additional scalar types from AND2, AND3, and higher-arity macros.
Adds the Dispatch_v2 header while retaining the existing dispatch header.
limitations: It does not compile or test converted code.
It targets PyTorch ATen C++ and CUDA source patterns.
Custom dispatch macros and unusual nested expressions may require manual review.
Build validation is still required to confirm behavior and type coverage.

use_cases.title: Modernize an ATen kernel
use_cases.description: Convert legacy dispatch calls in a native operator while preserving supported scalar types.

use_cases.title: Update a CUDA implementation
use_cases.description: Migrate CUDA kernel dispatch macros and wrap complex lambdas correctly.

use_cases.title: Review a dispatch migration
use_cases.description: Check argument order, type expansion, includes, and individual scalar types before review.

prompt_templates.title: Convert one macro
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert the AT_DISPATCH macro in [file path] to AT_DISPATCH_V2. Preserve its type coverage and show the changed section.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner is updating one dispatch call.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a kernel file
prompt_templates.prompt: Update every legacy AT_DISPATCH call in [file path]. Add the required header and summarize each type-group mapping.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer is migrating one ATen or CUDA file.

prompt_templates.title: Review an existing conversion
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the AT_DISPATCH_V2 conversions in [file path]. Check argument order, AT_WRAP placement, AT_EXPAND usage, and preserved individual types.
prompt_templates.scenario: A reviewer needs a focused migration audit.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a complex migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze all dispatch macros in [paths]. Propose conversions for combined type groups and complex lambdas, then identify cases needing manual validation.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced contributor is planning a multi-file migration.

output_examples.input: Convert one all-types dispatch call with three additional scalar types.
output_examples.output: Added the v2 dispatch header. Reordered the arguments, wrapped the lambda, expanded the all-types group, and preserved all three scalar types.

output_examples.input: Review a floating-type conversion in a CUDA kernel.
output_examples.output: The conversion preserves the floating group and additional low-precision types. The lambda wrapper and argument order are correct.

output_examples.input: Check a file containing combined integral and complex dispatch groups.
output_examples.output: The review identifies separate explicit type-group expansions and lists any custom type combinations requiring manual verification.

best_practices: Compare the legacy macro name and suffix with the final explicit type list.
Wrap the complete lambda and preserve its captures, body, and operation name.
Compile and test the affected target after applying the conversion.
anti_patterns: Do not expand individual scalar types with AT_EXPAND.
Do not remove the existing dispatch header without checking other uses.
Do not assume a textual conversion proves compilation or runtime behavior.

faq.question: Which macros can this skill convert?
faq.answer: It covers common all-types, floating, integral, complex, combined, and additional-type AT_DISPATCH patterns.

faq.question: Can it edit the source file?
faq.answer: Yes. Its workflow reads the target file, updates dispatch calls, and adds the v2 header when needed.

faq.question: Does it compile or test the result?
faq.answer: No. The skill focuses on conversion, so users must run the appropriate build and tests afterward.

faq.question: Why is AT_WRAP required?
faq.answer: AT_WRAP protects the lambda from macro parsing problems caused by internal commas.

faq.question: Does it support CUDA kernels?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance applies to ATen C++ files, CUDA kernels, and native operator implementations.

faq.question: How are extra scalar types preserved?
faq.answer: Types encoded by legacy AND suffixes become individual trailing arguments after the expanded type groups.
